title: Influence of the treatment protocol on the dental arch width and occlusal characteristics of 6-year-old patients with cleft lip and/or palate.
source: PubMed · Journal of cranio-maxillo-facial surgery : official publication of the European Association for Cranio-Maxillo-Facial Surgery
byline: Van Geneugden L, Verdonck A, Dormaar JT, et al.
html: The aim of this study was to compare the maxillary width and occlusal characteristics of six-year-old patients with cleft lip and/or palate treated with two different surgical protocols. Six-year-old patients with cleft palate (CP), unilateral cleft lip and palate (UCLP), and bilateral cleft lip and palate (BCLP) treated with protocol A (soft palate closure at 1 year using a modified Veau-Wardill-Kilner pushback technique, and hard palate closure between 5 and 7 years using the von Langenbeck procedure) or protocol B (soft palate closure at 1 year using Sommerlad intravelar veloplasty, and hard palate closure with a vomer flap at the time of lip repair) were included. A non-cleft control group was used for comparison. Maxillary and mandibular arch width, maxillary arch length, dental arch relationship, sagittal molar occlusion, overjet, overbite, and crossbite prevalence were assessed. Groups were compared using non-parametric tests and proportional odds models. In total, 134 patients (58 CP, 51 UCLP, and 25 BCLP) were included: 79 treated with protocol A and 55 with protocol B. Eighty-one controls were included. No statistically significant differences were observed between the two protocols for most outcomes, although protocol B required fewer treatment interventions.
